explanation: The later article's background is the march out of the captured port: “The French troops then marched on and assaulted Alexandria and captured it after its Wali, Koraim Pasha, refused to surrender. After capturing Alexandria, Napoleon sent a column eastwards to capture Rosetta … The main column of the French army was hurriedly marched out of Alexandria after a rest of less than two days, ordered by Napoleon to march some 50 miles across mostly barren terrain, aiming for Ramaniyah, a village on the banks of the Nile”, and its lead places the battle “on their march to Cairo”. The Pyramids article says the same thing in one sentence: “After landing in Ottoman-controlled Egypt and capturing Alexandria on 2 July 1798, the French army under General Bonaparte marched across the desert toward Cairo.” `precondition-of` and not `caused`: Alexandria is the base the march was launched from and the supply line that made it possible, not the reason Murad Bey stood at Shubra Khit. Probable: Wikipedia alone.
